about.title: Ceres Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Ceres sits at the crossroads of agriculture, distribution, and light industry in Stanislaus County, and workplace injuries here run the gamut from warehouse falls to equipment accidents to vehicle collisions during work duties. Under California law, workers' compensation is typically the exclusive remedy against your own employer, no matter who was at fault. But that's not always the end of the story. If a subcontractor, property owner, delivery driver, or equipment manufacturer contributed to your injury, you may have a separate claim against that third party, one that can provide compensation workers' comp doesn't cover. Given how many Ceres jobs involve driving on corridors like Whitmore Avenue and Mitchell Road, or working alongside outside contractors, third-party exposure is common. LawProactive doesn't provide legal advice or represent you directly, but we can connect you free of charge with an independent attorney who can sort out which paths apply to your situation and help you move forward without added stress.

items.desc: Workers' comp is usually your exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party like a contractor or equipment maker can still be liable separately. An independent attorney can evaluate whether your injury involves both paths.

items.title: We Understand the Reporting Clock
items.desc: California generally requires injured workers to report a workplace injury to their employer within 30 days. Missing that window can complicate your comp claim, so getting guidance early matters.

items.title: We Know Retaliation Is Illegal
items.desc: California law prohibits employers from retaliating against workers who report an injury or pursue a claim. If you're worried about your job, an independent attorney can help you understand your protections.

items.question: I was hurt on a job in Ceres by a subcontractor's equipment. Can I sue them separately from filing workers' comp?
items.answer: Possibly. While workers' comp generally covers claims against your own employer regardless of fault, a negligent third party like a subcontractor may be separately liable for your injury. An independent attorney connected through LawProactive can review the details and explain whether a third-party claim, which carries a 2-year deadline in California, applies to your situation.

items.question: How long do I have to report my injury to my employer in Ceres?
items.answer: California law generally requires you to report a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days. Reporting promptly helps preserve your workers' comp claim and creates a record close to when the incident happened, which can matter later. If you're unsure how to report it, an independent attorney can walk you through the process.

items.question: My employer hinted I'd be let go if I filed a claim. Is that legal in Ceres or anywhere in California?
items.answer: No, retaliation against an employee for reporting a workplace injury or filing a claim is illegal under California law. If you're experiencing pressure like this, it's worth talking to an independent attorney who can explain your protections and options. LawProactive can connect you with one at no cost.
